note:
Paper 73, Team 35532. Fifty-nine measured regions over twenty-seven of the thirty-four pages, all fifty-nine accounted for: twenty-eight exhibit regions - thirteen numbered figures, the two uncaptioned delivery-plan bands, and thirteen tables - and thirty-one exclusions, so unaccounted is zero and nothing is left unresolved. Seventeen exclusions are inner rasters of framed plots, eight are prose or equation bands, four are the tails of tables that break across a page, one is the band that carries three caption strips, and one is the abstract's last lines. The paper numbers thirteen figures and nine tables; every figure is here, and eight of the nine tables are rows because Table 6 shares p22's measured box with Table 5.

The measuring defect on this paper is new to the lane and shapes the whole census. The PDF draws a set of thin rules around every individual line of type, so a paragraph or a display equation comes out as a page-wide vector region, and the running-head rule at y=65.5 drags those boxes out to the full 415.4 pt measure. Nothing mechanical separates them from real exhibits: the white-fill discriminator used on the previous paper returns nothing usable here, and area buys nothing either, since a prose band reaches 0.59 of the page while the p27 delivery band that holds four exhibits reaches 0.21. Every rejection on this paper was made by looking at the render, and the eight not-an-exhibit rows are all prose with the page-top rule as their only drawn mark.

Every pasted plot is framed by vector rules after it was pasted, so the container and its content are two regions. Where the frame holds one plot - Figs 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 - the frame is the row and the raster is excluded; where it holds three separately numbered plots, as on p8, the three rasters are the rows and the frame is excluded as the band carrying their caption strips. The result is that this census records thirteen figures from fifteen figure regions plus two composite bands, and seventeen regions of pasted bitmap that are not exhibits in their own right.

What the exhibits are. Nine line plots carry the two model fits, the drug-production curve, the two sensitivity sweeps and the control-time curve; two are flow charts - the four-box SEIR cartoon of Fig.1 and the five-box SEIIR cartoon of Fig.3; two are the Sierra Leone district maps of Figs 6 and 7; two are the uncaptioned delivery-plan bands of pp27-28; and thirteen are grids. The line plots are pasted Matlab bitmaps throughout: Fig.4 and Fig.5 each hold two panels with their own legends inside the axes, and Fig.5's two legends map the same colour to opposite cases, so 'with drug' is the blue curve on one panel and the green curve on the other and nothing on the page resolves it.

The quietest failure is the delivery plan. Six monthly plans are introduced by one sentence - 'We get our delivery plan for six month shown as following table and figure.' - and none of the six is numbered: two plots and two grids on p27, four plots and four grids on p28, every grid 3 rows by 4 columns of country, infected case, death case and portion, with 'Sierra Leone' wrapping onto a second line in every one of them and the word 'Leone' colliding with the bottom rule at the lower left of p28. The header of those grids breaks mid-word, reading 'Infect' over 'ed' over 'case', so the column cannot be read as one label. None of the six carries a scale, a legend or a unit on either plot.

The tables carry their own damage. The three symbol lists run to five slices across pp2-4 with the header printed only twice, and the slices disagree with themselves: the open-degree row is defined twice in a row on p4 with C_n repeating F_n's own wording, G(t) wraps onto a second line so the list reads as six short rows, and three definitions in a row are cut mid-sentence. Table 5's header disagrees with its own body - 'current disease situation' stands over 2917 and 'Population density' over 45.5 - and Table 4's unit note stops at 'People /per km' after item 1 of what should be four. In Table 2 several distances are broken across two lines inside their cell, so 227 prints as '22' over '7' and 309 as '30' over '9'. Table 9's header reads 'The days use / to control' and never says what the last column is, and its cells mix bare counts with bracketed percentages so a reader cannot tell the changed input from the outcome; the sentence that follows it also cites 'Table 2' instead of Table 9. Table 8's last row reports a death case of 119556 against an initial value an order of magnitude smaller, and the caption of Table 8 has its baseline struck through by the top rule of its own grid.

On the figure side, Fig.1 draws four compartments S, E, I and R while the text beside it says an infectious individual 'either recover and survive R or die D', so the cartoon has no D at all. Fig.3's box letters are bitmaps pasted next to vector edge labels and sit visibly ragged against them. Fig.6's choropleth encodes nothing - all twelve districts carry one flat pink fill - so the map is only a key to district names and shapes, and its caption ends in a dangling 'Source:' with nothing after the colon. Fig.7 reuses the same fill and collides its district names with seven red star markers. Fig.8's y tick numbers are rotated unreadably, Fig.9's x axis label 'Beta' is cut off at its right end and its caption has lost its own title, and Fig.10's caption has lost its beginning - only 'creases, and death cases increases' survives, which is the tail of the prose sentence above it. Fig.11 is labelled by nothing but a bare 'Fig.11' under the art, so the paper's last figure has no title at all.

Citation practice is thin. Sixteen of the twenty-eight exhibit rows are named in the prose and each is cited exactly once; twelve are never named - the three p8 plots, the two delivery bands, the five symbol slices, Table 4 and Table 5. Three citations point backwards across a page break, Table 3 by six pages, which is why lead_pages is negative there. The prose also loses its own pointer in two places: 'shown in Table' for Table 6 without the number, and 'shown Table 3' for Table 3 without the preposition.

The heading layer is worse than the prose. The pass that builds the section index missed 'Model I' on p5, 'Model II' on p13 and 'Results & analysis' on p25, and invented a heading '2 December' out of a date in the data prose, so the paths recorded here use the printed lines the pass dropped. Three printed captions have no space after their number - 'Fig.2.1the early EBOV transmission period of Guinea', 'Table4:the data of the different district', 'Table 9 The days use' - and the caption vocabulary has no lower-case or unpunctuated form, so the nearest form is recorded and the printing itself is described on each row.
rules: Full width means 75 per cent or more of this paper's own 415.4 pt measure: the narrowest recorded grid is Table 9 at 80.5 per cent and the widest is the p22 band at 102.2, so all thirteen tables are full and none is half, while the figures run from a 47.7 per cent sensitivity plot to the 102.2 per cent Fig.4 [table.width].

This PDF draws four thin rules around every single line of type, so prose bands and display equations arrive as page-wide measured regions - the page-header rule at y=65.5 stretches a band's box to the full text measure. The white-fill test that separated prose from exhibits on an earlier paper returns nothing here, so the eight not-an-exhibit and the four split-across-pages rejections were made by looking at the render, not by an area or fill threshold [place.area_frac].

Every pasted plot arrives as a bitmap inside a drawn frame, and most frames carry the caption as a second, separate bitmap strip, so the frame is the exhibit row and the seventeen inner rasters are excluded as fragments of it rather than counted as seventeen more exhibits [place.page_order].

Two printed floats can share one measured box: on p22 Table 5 and Table 6 sit one above the other inside a single region, and the census can carry that box only once, so Table 6 - three body rows, two columns, horizontal rules only, introduced by a sentence that loses its own number at 'shown in Table' - is recorded in words on the Table 5 row and is not a row of its own [table.rows].

Rows counts body rows only, never the header: the p2 symbol slice is 7 rows, the p3 slices 9 and 12, the p4 slices 8 and 10, Table 1 is 5 body rows although only 1 prints beside its caption, and the delivery-plan grids are 3 body rows each [table.rows].

Rule style is read literally: boxed means a closed four-sided frame, which only Table 2 and Table 7 have; vertical-rules means horizontal rules with an internal vertical divider and open left and right edges, which is ten of the thirteen; booktabs means horizontal rules alone, which is Table 8 [table.rule_style].

Eight grids continue onto a following page with the header not repeated and no continuation mark - the four symbol slices on pp3-4, Table 1, Table 2, Table 4 and Table 8 - so continued is true on the row that keeps the header and the tail is excluded as split-across-pages instead of becoming a second table [table.continued].

A box that holds two or more different families and no caption and no number is one composite-panel row, not two rows: the p27 band is two plots above two grids and the p28 band is four plots and four grids, and neither carries a number the paper ever explains [geometry.panel_count].

Position splits by exhibit type without exception - all eight numbered table rows print their caption above the grid and all thirteen numbered figures print theirs below the art - and the two uncaptioned composite rows and the five symbol slices keep the default while caption_source stays none [caption.position].

The printed caption forms have no single convention - 'Fig.2.1the', 'Fig. 9:', 'Table.3', 'Table4:the', 'Table 5: the', bare 'Fig.11' and bare 'Table 9' all occur, three of them with no space after the number - so numbering records the nearest vocabulary form and the exact printing is described per row [caption.numbering].

Three exhibits are named in the prose before the page they print on - Table 3 six pages early, Table 8 and Fig.10 one page early - so lead_pages is negative on those three rows and first_page points backwards; twelve of the twenty-eight exhibit rows are never named in the prose at all [mention.lead_pages].

Section paths follow the printed heading above the block, including three the heading pass missed - 'Model I' on p5, 'Model II' on p13 and 'Results & analysis' on p25 - which are accepted because each is a printed line of the text layer [place.section_path].

Note sentences are quoted from the layer that introduces the grid, which is why two of them carry the paper's own breakage: 'Measuring the need of every district hi' and 'we final get data needed from the website of World Bank' [table.note_sentence].

tables.note: The list has no number and no caption; its only title is the heading 'Symbols and definitions' at the foot of p2. Header 'Symbol | definitions', seven rows S through D, a rule under the header and one at the bottom, a single internal vertical rule after the symbol column, and alternating grey shading; left and right stay open. It is the first slice of one list that runs unrepeatedly over three pages.

Second slice of the same symbol list: nine rows from N to G(t), header not repeated, so the reader has to turn back to p2 for the column titles. Same vertical rule and grey zebra; the mu definition wraps onto a second line.

Third slice, opened by the clipped sub-caption '(2)Symbol for model II' (the text layer reads 'ymbol for model II'). Header repeated, twelve rows, same single vertical rule and grey zebra. The distance definition drops its leading t and reads 'he shortest distance between', r_n and m_n carry stray semicolons, and I_n's definition stops mid-sentence.
Fourth slice: eight rows, header not repeated, same vertical rule and zebra. The open degree row is defined twice - F_n and then C_n repeating F_n's own wording - and J_n ends with a stray 'i'.

Last slice, under the clipped sub-caption '(3)Symbol for model III'. Header repeated, ten rows, this one closing the list. t_n and the isolated-infectious row wrap onto second lines, which is why three wrapped definitions in a row read as six short rows.
